test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following schemes aims at fostering innovation & technology development in defence and aerospace by engaging start-ups, MSMEs, academic institutes under the management of the Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)?

options.text: Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX

solution:
The correct answer is __**Innovations for Defence Excellence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX)** was launched by the **Prime Minister** of India in **April 2018** during the **DefExpo**.
 
• It serves as the flagship initiative of the **Ministry of Defence** to encourage **innovation** and **technology development** specifically for the **Defence and Aerospace** sectors.
 
• The scheme is managed and funded by the **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO)**, which was formed as a **not-for-profit** company under **Section 8** of the **Companies Act 2013**.
 
• The primary objective of **iDEX** is to engage various stakeholders, including **start-ups**, **MSMEs**, **individual innovators**, and **academic institutions**, to develop cutting-edge technologies for the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• It provides **grants** and **funding** to carry out **Research and Development (R&D)** projects that have a high potential for future adoption by the **Indian Army**, **Navy**, and **Air Force**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO):**
 
 
• The **DIO** was founded by two major **Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs)**, namely **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)** and **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**.
 
• It acts as the executive body that oversees the implementation of the **iDEX** framework and ensures the efficient utilization of the **Defence Innovation Fund**.
 
 
 
• **Technology Development Fund (TDF):**
 
 
• The **Technology Development Fund (TDF)** is a program executed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**.
 
• It aims to support **MSMEs** and **start-ups** in developing components, products, and systems that are currently not available in the **Indian defence** industry.
 
• Unlike **iDEX**, which focuses on broader innovation, **TDF** is more specifically aligned with **DRDO's** mission of **indigenization**.
 
 
 
• **Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX (ADITI):**
 
 
• The **ADITI** scheme was launched in **March 2024** during the **DefConnect 4.0** event to promote innovations in **critical and strategic defence technologies**.
 
• It offers a much higher grant-in-aid of up to **Rs 25 crore** to **start-ups** for research and development in areas like **space technology** and **cybersecurity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC):** Under the **iDEX** initiative, the **DISC** is periodically launched to present specific problem statements from the **Armed Forces** to the **start-up ecosystem**.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** The core vision of these schemes is to achieve **Atmanirbharta** (self-reliance) in **defence production** and reduce India's dependency on **foreign imports**.
 
• **iDEX Prime:** This is an extension of **iDEX** meant to support projects requiring higher funding, offering grants up to **Rs 10 crore** for more complex **technological challenges**.
 
• **Financial Support:** Since its inception, **iDEX** has supported hundreds of **start-ups** and led to the procurement of various **indigenous technologies** by the **Indian military**.
</ul
